to be honest

everyday the past couple months I've thought about quitting and shutting down oasis.

i’ve never believed more in oasis: my consumer health startup powered by transparent product testing, but...

our revenue is down 85% since april this year and our legal bills keep growing

a billion-dollar cpg company is suing us for $255 million over a social post where we incorrectly stated the amount of heavy metals in their electrolytes. we corrected it within 24 hours and offered to boost the correction to reach the same audience. their legal team said they weren’t interested.

our defense costs tens of thousands a month to present our case and could reach 6 or 7 figures if the case continues without a settlement

the odds are stacked against us. without outside help, i’m honestly unsure how we get through this

yet I cant get myself to stop. and neither can our team, who have chosen to keep working without pay. 

oasis has never been better, faster, and backed by more verified lab data with our social content now being exclusively positive.

we’ve also launched consumer and brand testing so shoppers can test their own products and brands can improve their quality and oasis scores.

revenue isn’t down because customers don’t love the product. in fact, our conversion rates are among the highest of any consumer health platform. it's because we put our remaining resources into engineering, science, and independent lab testing.

we also take time to share accurate, valuable information that benefits our community long term, rather than chase downloads with inaccurate slop.

earlier this year, with a growth team, we did well. now I handle all growth and content myself to cut costs.

i and so many of our customers and team, believe the world is better with oasis in it.

we haven’t operated perfectly this year. no company pursuing a big mission does, but we’ve listened to all feedback and improved accordingly.

i’m not sharing this to ask for pity, but rather for 2 reasons:

1. to show what founding a company can feel like behind the scenes: difficult, uncertain and sometimes terrifying

2. to possibly reach the right people who can help us survive and help us carry on the mission of empowering consumers and raising the health standard for everyone.
